issues.location: definition, inverse proof and half-group partition of the planar rotation group
issues.finding: Rotations through rational radian values in [0,2pi) are not closed under composition or inversion modulo 2pi, since 2pi is irrational. The later half-group squaring claim requires rational multiples of a full turn; the zero-angle inverse also needs separate handling under the chosen interval convention.
issues.proposed_resolution: Define the group by angles that are rational multiples of a full turn represented in [0,2pi), carry that qualification into both halves and the orbit description, and note that the identity is self-inverse.

issues.location: partition of D_1 by images of the choice set
issues.finding: The proof indexes its D_1 pieces by rho in R_1, a symbol not defined here; the defined first half of the rotation group is rotationsgroup_1.
issues.proposed_resolution: Index those pieces by rho in rotationsgroup_1.

issues.location: definition of measure and final nonmeasurability proof on source lines 240--267
issues.finding: The text treats any real-valued countably additive assignment as a measure without stating nonnegativity or closure of the measurable domain under rotations, although both are used in the concluding contradiction. The proof also quantifies rotations rho over the choice set C twice, despite C containing points, not rotations.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use a nonnegative measure on a rotation-invariant measurable domain, explain nonmeasurability relative to that domain, and quantify the two rotation variables over rotationsgroup.

translation_treatment: The target repairs the rotation group definition and zero-angle inverse, the first-half index, and the normalized invariant-measure argument; it localizes the mathematical iff and four citation locators. The frozen source remains unchanged.
